title: Hotfix orchestration for rolling model regressions affecting Hosted, Dedicated, and Private deployments
creator: Maya Chen
description:
Summary:
On 2026-03-04 22:14 UTC a canary rollout of model-v3.2.1 triggered a measurable regression for multiple customer workloads: increased hallucination rate on search/rerank prompts and a ~15% spike in tail latency for long-context chat sessions. Incidents came in from Hosted (redwood-api), two Dedicated customers (AcmeHealth, RetailFlow), and one Private customer (EduFlow) that had run the optional 'apply-latest-model' script. Dashboards (console -> runtime -> model-health) showed divergence on the eval prompt set and automated quality alerts fired at 22:10 UTC.

What we believe happened:
- Model v3.2.1 conversion introduced a subtle tokenization offset in the conversion toolchain that changed prompt framing for multi-turn contexts.
- The runtime kernel scheduling change in runtime-1.20 made a corner-case batching path more aggressive, exposing the token alignment issue on production traffic.
- Canary traffic weighting allowed the regression to reach 8-12% of traffic across some routes before operator alerts.

Immediate mitigation taken:
1) Paused the global canary at 22:30 UTC for hosted.
2) Rolled back hosted production pool to model-v3.2.0 at 22:50 UTC (rollback PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pull/2768).
3) Opened dedicated rollback requests for affected customers (AcmeHealth, RetailFlow) and coordinated with account owners to apply v3.2.0 rollback to their reserved pools; both rollbacks completed by 23:40 UTC.
4) Notified Private customer EduFlow and provided a rollback script (private-rollback-edu.sh) and assisted via remote session; they applied rollback at 00:05 UTC.
5) Disabled the aggressive batching path via runtime config flag runtime.batch_aggressive=false as a short-term mitigation for further risk surface.

Root cause (initial):
- Primary: model conversion pipeline (model-tools v0.9.7 -> v0.9.8) introduced a token offset for certain multi-token special tokens used by our prompt templates. This was not caught by unit tests which only used short-context templates.
- Secondary: a change in kernel scheduling exposed the misalignment on high-length sequences.

Owners and communications:
- Incident lead (triage): Arjun Patel (assignee)
- Runtime SRE: Priya Nair (oncall)
- Model Ops: Daniel Ortiz
- PM escalation contact: Clara Gomez
- Customer success liaison: Jenna Park
- Slack incident channel: #incident-model-regressions (internal)
- Pagerduty incident: PD-6421
- Confluence incident doc: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/INFR/ENG-16401

Planned permanent fixes:
- Revert the tokenization change in model-tools and publish v0.9.9 that preserves prior token alignment OR add a compatibility shim in the conversion step (PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/model-tools/pull/2791).
- Harden unit + integration tests: add long-context and multi-turn templates to conversion test harness and nightly evals.
- Add a pre-deploy diff step that runs the canonical eval prompt suite against canary candidates; fail canary rollout if quality delta > 1.5% on core evals.
- Runtime: tune batching threshold heuristics and add telemetry that flags sudden alignment-drift signals.

Rollout coordination plan (short):
- Block all automated canary promotions until v3.2.1 candidate passes expanded conversion tests.
- For Hosted: require a successful canary run of 72 hours on the canonical eval set with no regression before re-promote.
- For Dedicated: provide an opt-in staged promotion plan and a one-click rollback script in Console for customers to revert with minimal downtime.
- For Private: ship patch to model-tools and a signed rollback/hotfix bundle; coordinate with customer SAs and schedule maintenance windows.

Follow-ups / action items (owners):
- Arjun: Drive hotfix PR and coordinate rollback confirmations across customers (status: in-progress).
- Daniel (Model Ops): Author conversion test additions and land model-tools PR (#2791) by 2026-03-12 (status: in-review).
- Priya (SRE): Add alignment-drift alert to console and increase retention for model-eval logs (status: blocked on infra quota).
- Clara (PM): Notify top-5 affected customers with incident summary and ETA for permanent fix (status: done).
- Jenna (CS): Run 1:1 post-recovery check-ins with AcmeHealth and EduFlow (status: scheduled).

Risk & customer notes:
- Several Dedicated customers rely on pinned versions; however, those who had automated 'apply-latest' scripts were impacted. We should discourage that pattern until we have canary-quality gates.
- SLA impact: AcmeHealth reported a degraded P99 latency above their threshold during the canary window and will likely request credit; keep support/finance in the loop.

- Engineering postmortem with action items and owners: 2026-03-20 (all owners)
